args.text: MPC-Diffusion is a training-free planner that treats denoising as a controlled dynamical system and, at each step, optimizes a short-horizon schedule of per-pixel control weights and latent adjustments to satisfy heterogeneous constraints while keeping a KL trust-region to the base denoiser. We linearize the score/denoiser around the current sample via low-rank Jacobian probes and solve a tiny quadratic program with slack and dual warm-starts in a receding-horizon loop; controls can be adapter features and differentiable losses (edge/depth/mask/flow) gated by cross-attention text masks. Compared to per-step arbitration or consensus-only schemes, the lookahead reduces control conflicts and mode collapse, improving constraint satisfaction under disagreement while preserving diversity; an optional amortized policy distills MPC solutions into a lightweight router for fast sampling. The planner also unifies multi-crop/tiling by scheduling future tiles and steps jointly, complementing MultiDiffusion-style fusers.

args.text: We propose Pareto-Guided Budgeted Diffusion (PGBD), an offline safe RL sampler that enforces dynamic episodic cost budgets by composing multi-objective diffusion guidance at decision time. At each diffusion step, we learn intermediate energy corrections via contrastive energy prediction for reward, safety reachability, and behavior-closeness, and choose their coefficients with an SDMGrad-like proximal rule to produce a common descent direction that satisfies the specified budget. This unifies TREBI’s budget conditioning and FISOR’s feasibility via reachability with principled, stepwise guidance, while a Diffusion-DICE score decomposition keeps proposals in-distribution. Paired with efficient single-/few-step EDP-style denoising, PGBD aims for zero violations inside the feasible set and sharp reward–safety trade-offs as budgets tighten.

result.text: The paper tackles the bottleneck that visual and vision-language representation learning depends on expensive, curated datasets by asking whether massive, noisy web-scale image–text pairs can substitute for careful curation. result.text: We tackle the residual verification bottleneck in lossless speculative decoding: even with improved drafting and joint block checks, the target model frequently runs full forward passes to accept drafts, which dominates latency in long-context, large-batch regimes. Our key insight is Certified Partial Verification (CPV): replace many full verifications with certified partial ones that propagate tight, precomputed layer-wise Lipschitz bounds and Jacobian–vector products to produce upper/lower bounds on target logits for a drafted block; when these bounds certify that the block-verification/optimal-transport acceptance would succeed, we accept without executing the remaining layers, else we fall back to exact verification. CPV preserves the exact-sample guarantee because acceptance occurs only under formal certificates, and when combined with joint block verification and KV-optimized serving it reduces target invocations on “easy” proposals to yield additional end-to-end speedups. A practical design amortizes bound computation across the batch and reuses cached per-prompt sensitivities, making CPV complementary to current block-verification and MagicDec-style systems.

result.text: The paper addresses inefficient and imbalanced token-to-expert routing in sparsely-activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where fixed top-k routing can leave experts under- or over-trained and tokens unfairly limited in expert access. The key insight is to reverse the selection direction—have experts choose the top-k tokens to serve rather than forcing tokens to pick a fixed number of experts—so each expert maintains a fixed bucket size while tokens can be routed to a variable number of experts, improving load balance and utilization. The method implements this “expert choice” routing within heterogeneous MoEs, compares it to prior top-1 and top-2 gating schemes under equal computational budgets, and demonstrates that expert choice yields over 2× faster pretraining convergence and better downstream fine-tuning performance on GLUE/SuperGLUE tasks, and even outperforms a dense T5 baseline on several tasks at lower activation cost.

result.text: The paper addresses safe offline reinforcement learning where a policy must respect dynamically determined, real-time safety budgets (constraint thresholds) without further environment interaction. The key insight is to treat the problem as one of conditioning trajectory distributions on varying episodic cost budgets and to use generative planning to produce trajectories that satisfy those budgets at decision time. result.text: The paper addresses the performance gap between low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full fine-tuning of foundation models, asking whether LoRA is being properly optimized. The key insight is that LoRA-based optimization is mathematically equivalent to full fine-tuning with a low-rank gradient, and that this low-rank gradient can be expressed directly from the gradients of LoRA’s two low-rank matrices; therefore, improving LoRA amounts to better approximating the full-fine-tuning gradient via adjustments to those matrix gradients. The authors propose LoRA-Pro, which derives and applies theoretically optimal adjustments to the low-rank matrix gradients so the resulting low-rank update more closely matches the full fine-tuning gradient, and they validate this approach across diverse tasks—showing substantial closing of the performance gap.

args.text: Fourier-Route: a training-free, frequency-selective arbitration layer for composable control in text-to-image diffusion. At each denoising step, we decompose both the UNet’s predicted noise and each control’s residual/guidance into a Laplacian pyramid, then solve a per-pixel, per-band simplex to allocate high-frequency budget to edges/flow and low-frequency budget to depth/segmentation/text, regularized by an energy-smoothing prior inspired by smoothed energy guidance. We also treat self-guidance vectors extracted from the frozen model as pseudo-controls and fuse them alongside adapter/ControlNet features, while MultiDiffusion-style tiling uses the same per-band weights to maintain consistency across crops and aspect ratios. This yields sharper structure without texture leakage and more stable global layout under conflicting controls, while remaining modular with Uni-ControlNet/T2I-Adapter backbones and compatible with existing consensus/routers.

result.text: Hardware-Aware Robust PEFT proposes jointly selecting per-layer low-rank adapter ranks and structured sparse adapter masks (e.g., n:m patterns like 2:4) to meet a specified latency or energy target on a given accelerator while minimizing the gap to full fine-tuning. We cast adapter configuration as a speedup-constrained allocation with device-measured per-layer cost models, solving a knapsack-like objective over discrete ranks and sparsity patterns using dynamic programming to maximize an accuracy proxy under the hardware budget. During training, we use a RoSA-style low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition with hardware-friendly sparsity, apply LoRA-Pro-inspired gradient corrections to better match the full fine-tuning gradient, and periodically resample low-rank projections as in Flora to realize higher effective rank without extra optimizer state. This yields PEFT configurations with predictable on-device speedups and strong accuracy, enabled by sparse kernels tuned to the chosen structured patterns.

The key insight is that hard safety constraints can be reformulated via reachability analysis as identifying the largest feasible region supported by the dataset, turning the original tri-objective into a feasibility-dependent objective that maximizes reward inside the feasible region and minimizes risk outside it. Building on this, the authors propose FISOR (FeasIbility-guided Safe Offline RL), which decouples constraint adherence, reward optimization, and behavior regularization into three processes and shows the optimal policy takes the form of a weighted behavior cloning solution. To extract that policy efficiently they introduce an energy-guided diffusion model that avoids training a time-dependent classifier, simplifying training while empirically ensuring zero violations across tasks and achieving top returns on the DSRL benchmark.

We propose Axiomatic Counterfactual Structure-Contrast (ACSC): a CLIP-style pretraining that learns explicit counterfactual operators over scene graphs and embeddings, constrained by Pearl-style axioms (composition, reversibility, effectiveness) under minimal graph edits. args.text: Receding-Horizon Control Arbitration for diffusion aims to overcome myopic, per-step weighting of heterogeneous controls by planning control weights a few steps ahead. At each denoising step, it performs a short predictive rollout (2–3 steps) using a cheap local linearization of the base score update and control-guidance effects, then solves a per-pixel simplex-constrained optimization that minimizes predicted cumulative control losses plus a trust-region regularizer to stay close to prior weights. Uncertainty-aware terms (from score variance and self-guidance signals) temper aggressive controls, while a MultiDiffusion-style consensus shares the same rollout across overlapping tiles to remain consistent on large canvases. This training-free, drop-in strategy stabilizes conflicting controls and better preserves text semantics by optimizing for future, not just instantaneous, constraint satisfaction.

result.text: The paper tackles slow speculative decoding for LLM inference, where a smaller draft model currently generates tokens autoregressively and spends equal time on all tokens, causing inefficiencies and limited speedups. The proposed Cascade Speculative Drafting (CS Drafting) introduces a Vertical Cascade that replaces neural autoregressive token-by-token generation with parallel or non-autoregressive drafting, and a Horizontal Cascade that dynamically prioritizes and allocates drafting time to more important or uncertain tokens; combined, these cascades let the target model accept larger portions of drafts less frequently and thus run fewer iterations. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of quantization in neural image compression, where common differentiable approximations (additive uniform noise, straight-through estimator, soft-to-hard annealing) either produce a train-test mismatch or weaken latent representation and degrade rate–distortion performance. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of encoding signals or scenes that contain a wide range of spatial frequencies with MLP-based neural implicit representations: standard positional encodings either use high frequencies that inject noise into smooth regions or low frequencies that fail to capture fine detail. The key insight is to expose an MLP to positional encodings progressively—feeding incrementally higher-frequency bands into a hierarchical network—so the model learns a hierarchy of detail levels without needing explicit supervision for each scale. Methodologically, the authors design a modular, multi-level MLP architecture where each level receives an increasing set of frequency encodings and produces a continuous implicit representation for its scale; levels can be used independently for coarser reconstructions and are trained jointly to improve accuracy, capacity, and convergence speed on 2D and 3D reconstruction tasks.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of achieving full fine-tuning (FFT) accuracy for large language models under tight computational and memory constraints by improving parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). Its key insight is that model updates can be decomposed into a jointly trained low-rank component and a highly sparse component—drawing on robust PCA ideas—so that their combination more faithfully approximates FFT than either low-rank or sparse updates alone. The proposed method, Robust Adaptation (RoSA), trains these two components on top of frozen pretrained weights and is supported by sparse GPU kernels and compatibility with low-precision base weights, yielding a practical system that outperforms LoRA, pure sparse, and other hybrid PEFTs at the same parameter budget and can recover FFT performance on some generative tasks.

result.text: Amortized Single-Sample Prompting (ASP) for CTTA: instead of maintaining per-domain prompt coresets, train a conditional hypernetwork that maps a single test image to a visual prompt for a frozen backbone, enabling per-sample adaptation with a single forward pass. We meta-train this prompt generator with an ARM-style objective that simulates domain shifts and minimizes expected post-adaptation risk, while imposing a homeostasis-inspired decomposition that gates domain-agnostic vs domain-specific prompt channels to preserve invariant knowledge. For nonstationary streams, we attach a tiny key–value memory of low-rank adapters for the prompt generator, updated online from short windows and retrieved by similarity, to rapidly snap back on revisits without overwriting the base. This combines the efficiency of prompt CTTA with the flexibility of single-sample adaptation and yields faster, lower-compute alignment than prompt coresets under brief, heterogeneous shifts.

args.text: We propose Belief-Conditioned Safety-Guided Diffusion for offline POMDPs with confounders and dynamic safety budgets. The method learns an object-centric SMC belief model to maintain multi-hypothesis latent states, then trains a budget-conditioned diffusion policy over action sequences whose guidance energy approximates reach-avoid feasibility in belief space computed from offline data; intermediate guidance is learned via contrastive energy prediction, while guided diffusion with in-sample distribution ratios keeps sampling on-distribution. At decision time, the planner samples multiple budget-conditioned candidate plans and selects using a pessimistic, proximal-causal value estimator over beliefs, while policy extraction leverages advantage-weighted updates to improve beyond behavior without querying OOD actions. This unifies feasibility-decoupled safe offline RL, diffusion planning, and confounder-robust POMDP learning to deliver zero-violation behavior and strong returns under real-time safety constraints.

result.text: The paper tackles the scarcity of paired image-text counterfactuals for evaluating and improving multimodal models' robustness to spurious correlations by proposing a scalable automatic construction method. The key insight is that text-to-image diffusion models can be guided to produce minimally changed images corresponding to counterfactual caption edits, enabling large-scale, realistic paired counterfactuals without costly manual collection. The authors implement this by editing MS-COCO captions to create targeted counterfactual descriptions and then using diffusion-based image generation and localized editing to synthesize matching counterfactual images, validating quality with human judgments, showing existing vision-language models struggle on these examples, and demonstrating that augmenting training data with COCO-Counterfactuals improves out-of-domain generalization.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of image compression by proposing an alternative to traditional pixel-based or learned-codebook methods that instead represents an image implicitly. The key insight is that overfitting a small multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to map continuous pixel coordinates to RGB values produces a compact, continuous representation whose learned weights encode the image and can be quantized to form a compressed code; this implicit neural representation can outperform JPEG at low bitrates even without entropy coding. The method fits an MLP per image, quantizes and stores the network weights as the compressed file, and reconstructs the image by evaluating the MLP at each pixel, and the paper empirically demonstrates competitive low-rate performance and highlights desirable properties (e.g., continuous resolution and simplicity) suggesting potential for further development.

args.text: We propose Articulation- and Affordance-Aware Test-Time Co-Personalization (A3-TTCP), which augments Gaussian human–object co-personalization by endowing each object with a lightweight kinematic graph whose joint parameters are initialized from category priors and adapted jointly with the SMPL-X avatar via self-supervised render-and-compare. Contact cues and occlusion-consistency drive bundle-adjustment over human pose, object pose, and articulation, while a vision–language affordance head supplies part-level contact likelihoods and motion-axis priors that regularize which object parts can move and which hand surfaces should engage. We optimize on sliding keyframe windows with long-horizon factor-graph consistency, yielding crisper fingers, fewer interpenetrations, and correct part motions for tools (e.g., lids, scissors) under domain shift, without annotations at test time. Built atop EVA-style Gaussian avatars and prior TTP methods, A3-TTCP resolves contact and articulation ambiguities in challenging egocentric sequences like VISOR.

result.text: Hardware-Aware Robust PEFT proposes jointly selecting per-layer low-rank adapter ranks and structured sparse adapter masks (e.g., n:m patterns like 2:4) to meet a specified latency or energy target on a given accelerator while minimizing the gap to full fine-tuning. We cast adapter configuration as a speedup-constrained allocation with device-measured per-layer cost models, solving a knapsack-like objective over discrete ranks and sparsity patterns using dynamic programming to maximize an accuracy proxy under the hardware budget. During training, we use a RoSA-style low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition with hardware-friendly sparsity, apply LoRA-Pro-inspired gradient corrections to better match the full fine-tuning gradient, and periodically resample low-rank projections as in Flora to realize higher effective rank without extra optimizer state. This yields PEFT configurations with predictable on-device speedups and strong accuracy, enabled by sparse kernels tuned to the chosen structured patterns.

result.text: The paper addresses the lack of realistic convergence guarantees for Plug-and-Play (PnP) image restoration methods, which use learned denoisers as priors but often rely on restrictive assumptions or convex data terms. The key insight is to design the denoiser as a single gradient descent step on a learned functional, so that the overall scheme can be interpreted as a proximal-gradient solver for an explicit global objective; this lets the authors leverage nonconvex proximal-gradient convergence theory to ensure the iterates approach stationary points. Methodologically, they embed this "gradient-step denoiser" into a half-quadratic splitting PnP framework, train the neural-network-parameterized functional to act as a high-quality denoiser, and demonstrate empirically on deblurring, super-resolution and inpainting that the algorithm converges in practice and achieves state-of-the-art restoration performance.

result.text: The paper addresses zero-shot open-world object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), where an agent must find any instance of a described object in an unexplored 3D environment without object-specific rewards or demonstrations. The key insight is to repurpose image-goal navigation training by embedding goal images into a shared multimodal semantic space so that language descriptions can be projected into the same space, enabling semantic-goal navigation without object labels. Methodologically, they train agents on ImageNav using these multimodal embeddings in large unannotated 3D datasets (e.g., HM3D), then at test time map free-form language goals into the learned embedding space to guide navigation; experiments on Gibson, HM3D, and MP3D show consistent 4.2%–20.0% absolute success improvements over prior zero-shot approaches and generalization to compound and room-conditioned instructions.

result.text: The paper tackles offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL), where limited, often suboptimal pre-collected trajectories and sparse goal rewards make learning long-horizon goal-directed behaviors challenging. Its key insight is that a conditional diffusion model can generate high-quality multi-step plans by stitching together useful sub-trajectory segments from offline data when conditioned not only on the target goal but also on an estimated target value, enabling the synthesis of trajectories that exceed individual dataset snippets. The proposed method, SSD (Sub-trajectory Stitching with Diffusion), first relabels the offline dataset with goal and value estimates, then trains a conditional diffusion model to sample future state-action sequences given a goal and value, and finally uses the model to produce stitched long-horizon plans which are executed or refined by a model-based policy; experiments show state-of-the-art performance and successful composition of suboptimal segments into effective goal-reaching plans.

At verification time, KV-CSD propagates tight, layer/head-wise sensitivity bounds from approximate-to-exact KV (sparse/evicted plus a tiny recurrent summary) to produce logit intervals; when these certify that joint block/OT acceptance would succeed, we accept without reconstructing missing KV, otherwise we selectively restore the minimal KV slices (layers/heads/timesteps) indicated by bound slack and re-verify. The method designs two complementary prompt types—domain-specific prompts to encode current-domain characteristics and domain-agnostic prompts to retain shared knowledge—and introduces a homeostasis-based adaptation strategy that suppresses domain-sensitive parameters in the agnostic prompts to better learn invariant features. result.text: We propose Belief-Conditioned Safety-Guided Diffusion for offline POMDPs with confounders and dynamic safety budgets. The method learns an object-centric SMC belief model to maintain multi-hypothesis latent states, then trains a budget-conditioned diffusion policy over action sequences whose guidance energy approximates reach-avoid feasibility in belief space computed from offline data; intermediate guidance is learned via contrastive energy prediction, while guided diffusion with in-sample distribution ratios keeps sampling on-distribution. At decision time, the planner samples multiple budget-conditioned candidate plans and selects using a pessimistic, proximal-causal value estimator over beliefs, while policy extraction leverages advantage-weighted updates to improve beyond behavior without querying OOD actions. This unifies feasibility-decoupled safe offline RL, diffusion planning, and confounder-robust POMDP learning to deliver zero-violation behavior and strong returns under real-time safety constraints.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of poor compositional generalization in sequence-to-sequence models by formalizing semantic outputs as partially ordered sets (posets) and noting that standard decoders wrongly impose strict ordering. args.text: Make speculative drafting certifiability-aware: choose candidate tokens and block lengths that maximize the chance that joint block verification can be certified after only a few target layers. We reuse CPV-style layer-wise Lipschitz/JVP bounds to define an early-certification margin for a drafted block and plug this as the objective in a SpecTr/OT-style multi-candidate selection, preferring drafts whose logits are both probable and tightly bounded so they can be certified early; a cheap lookahead bound pass over the first L′ layers estimates the minimal layer needed for certification. Coupled with block verification and PEARL’s pre/post verification overlap, the verifier begins certifying the prefix as soon as its early-cert margin clears while the drafter continues extending the suffix, accepting immediately if certificates hold and otherwise falling back. result.text: Consensus-Control Diffusion: a training-free mechanism that, at each denoising step, unrolls a few iterations of a small consensus optimization (ADMM-style) to reconcile the base denoiser with multiple heterogeneous controls (edges/depth/segmentation/color/flow/text regions). Each control contributes either a differentiable guidance loss (e.g., optical-flow or mask consistency) or a latent proposal from a lightweight adapter; the consensus update blends these via spatially varying weights estimated from per-control uncertainty derived from score variance between conditional/unconditional and a degraded "bad-guide" ensemble. This yields per-pixel, per-timestep allocation of a control budget—structure-heavy pixels lean on visual controls while style/background lean on text—while multi-crop/tiling proposals are fused in the same consensus to support large canvases. The approach preserves diversity relative to strong CFG, improves constraint satisfaction over naive guidance, and remains modular and composable across new control types without retraining.

result.text: We propose Graph-Edit Contrastive Pretraining (GE-CoP) to address compositional brittleness in image–text models by grounding alignment in explicit relational structure. For each image–caption pair we parse the caption into a scene graph, generate counterfactual negatives via minimal graph edits (attribute swaps, relation inversions, entity substitutions expanded with knowledge-graph synonyms), and paraphrase them with an LLM to remove lexical artifacts; training uses a graph-edit-distance–weighted contrastive objective that enforces larger margins for more distant edits and a group-wise positive term that pulls together examples sharing a subgraph. We co-train a lightweight scene-graph head with cycle-consistency between text-derived and image-derived graphs to avoid reliance on perfect external parsers, and stabilize learning with a momentum teacher. This unifies hard, structure-aware negatives with structured priors and yields relation- and order-sensitive representations expected to improve ARO/SugarCrepe and relation-centric retrieval without hurting general CLIP transfer.

result.text: The paper addresses noisy and imperfect one-to-one image-text pairing in vision-language pretraining, where strict binary positives/negatives in contrastive CLIP training fails to capture many-to-many or partially matching relationships. result.text: I propose nullspace-aware cold re-noising for PnP: at each iteration, first project the estimate to the data-consistent affine set, decompose it into measurement-space and nullspace components, then apply a deterministic operator-conditioned cold corruption only in the nullspace (e.g., blur, masking, or spectral shrinkage aligned to A’s singular spectrum) before denoising with a learned proximal network trained under the same nullspace-only corruption. This preserves data consistency while reinstating diffusion-like regularization exactly along directions the likelihood cannot constrain, reducing hallucinations and improving stability. Because the denoiser is an exact proximal map and the nullspace corruption is nonexpansive, the composite update fits the nonconvex proximal-gradient theory, and we adapt corruption strength via a discrepancy principle tied to the residual. Instantiations for MRI (k-space line masking restricted to unmeasured coils/lines) and CT (angular subsampling within unmeasured views) accelerate convergence and improve perceptual fidelity relative to Gaussian re-noising.

result.text: The paper addresses the rigidity of neural image compression (NIC), where different rate-distortion (R-D) operating points typically require separate encoder-decoder pairs or inflexible conditional schemes, limiting practical deployment and adaptability. Its key insight is that variable bitrate and flexible coding goals can be achieved at inference time by "editing" a single latent code via semi-amortized optimization and adaptive quantization, rather than baking rate control into the network during training. The method performs semi-amortized inference to iteratively refine the latent representation for a given R-D target, applies adaptive, learnable quantization to adjust bitrate and distortion trade-offs, and thus enables variable-rate coding, region-of-interest (ROI) prioritization, and multi-distortion objectives with a single decoder. Experimental results demonstrate that this code-editing approach outperforms prior variable-rate NIC methods while providing much greater flexibility.

result.text: We tackle the residual verification bottleneck in lossless speculative decoding: even with improved drafting and joint block checks, the target model frequently runs full forward passes to accept drafts, which dominates latency in long-context, large-batch regimes. Our key insight is Certified Partial Verification (CPV): replace many full verifications with certified partial ones that propagate tight, precomputed layer-wise Lipschitz bounds and Jacobian–vector products to produce upper/lower bounds on target logits for a drafted block; when these bounds certify that the block-verification/optimal-transport acceptance would succeed, we accept without executing the remaining layers, else we fall back to exact verification. CPV preserves the exact-sample guarantee because acceptance occurs only under formal certificates, and when combined with joint block verification and KV-optimized serving it reduces target invocations on “easy” proposals to yield additional end-to-end speedups. result.text: The paper tackles the gap between parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods like LoRA and full fine-tuning, which often leads to underperformance on complex or domain-specific tasks. The key insight is that standard LoRA’s symmetric, uniform low-rank adapters are both training- and parameter-inefficient for challenging datasets, and that an asymmetric allocation of adapter capacity can better capture task-specific complexity without needing domain expertise. The authors propose HydraLoRA, an asymmetric LoRA architecture that redistributes low-rank components across layers and projection directions to match representational needs, and they validate it through experiments showing consistent gains over existing PEFT methods—including those that incorporate domain knowledge—while maintaining parameter efficiency.

result.text: The paper addresses the practical challenge in plug-and-play (PnP) proximal algorithms for inverse imaging—namely, the need for manual tuning of internal parameters (penalty weight, denoising strength, and stopping time) across varying imaging conditions and scene content. Its key insight is that a learned policy can automatically and adaptively select these parameters per state, yielding more efficient and effective convergence than fixed or handcrafted rules. The method implements a policy network trained with a hybrid of model-free and model-based deep reinforcement learning to control the PnP proximal iterations, and studies interactions with different pretrained denoisers to produce a tuning-free PnP scheme. Experiments on linear and nonlinear problems, including compressed sensing MRI and phase retrieval, show the learned policy customizes parameters per instance and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

result.text: The paper addresses the limitation of unsupervised test-time adaptation (TTA) under substantial distribution shifts by proposing active test-time adaptation (ATTA), which allows querying a limited number of labels from streaming test data to improve robustness. The key insight is that selectively acquiring a small set of labeled test instances can provably reduce generalization error across test domains and mitigate catastrophic forgetting compared to purely unsupervised TTA. To realize this, the authors derive learning-theoretic guarantees for ATTA, propose a sample-entropy balancing strategy to avoid forgetting, and introduce SimATTA, a lightweight real-time sample-selection algorithm that integrates label queries into TTA. Empirical evaluations across benchmarks show that SimATTA substantially outperforms standard TTA methods and approaches the performance of heavier active domain adaptation approaches while remaining efficient.

args.text: Tractable-Prior Arbitration (TPA): a training-free router for composable control that leverages a pretrained probabilistic circuit as a fast tractable prior over image layout and mid-level structure. At each denoising step, it scores each control locally by the circuit’s constrained posterior likelihood of the current latent patch if forced to satisfy that control, then solves a per-pixel (optionally per-frequency) simplex that minimizes control losses while regularizing toward the circuit posterior, thus downweighting implausible or out-of-distribution controls. A single ADMM-style consensus update blends the UNet step with these PC-weighted controls across MultiDiffusion tiles, improving global layout stability and conflict resolution without retraining. The router is compatible with ControlNet/Adapter backbones and frequency-selective routing, subsuming prior arbitration schemes while adding a data-driven plausibility prior.

We propose a bitrate‑scalable implicit image codec that trains per‑image INRs with a soft‑then‑hard weight quantization schedule that is frequency‑aware and ROI‑editable. During fitting, we inject scaled additive uniform noise into weight groups aligned with progressively enabled positional‑encoding bands and optimize a variational upper bound on coded weight rate to learn groupwise step sizes; we then switch to hard integer quantization and entropy‑code weights ordered by band to enable progressive decoding. Variable‑rate and ROI refinement are achieved at playback via semi‑amortized code editing that transmits sparse low‑rank adapter deltas for selected layers/regions, trading a few bits for localized fidelity without retraining or multiple decoders. Compared to post‑hoc weight quantization, this closes the train–test gap for INR codecs and reduces ringing on high‑frequency screen content while enabling on‑demand zoom at a fixed base bitrate.

result.text: We propose Contact-TTP, a contact-aware test-time personalization method for expressive human pose and shape that improves hand–object and foot–ground plausibility under domain shift without annotations. Starting from a ViT-based EHPS foundation model, we attach lightweight adapters and adapt per-person/per-scene using self-supervised objectives that attract SMPL-X mesh vertices to detected contact regions (hands–objects, feet–ground), penalize interpenetration, and enforce short-horizon temporal consistency. Contact likelihoods are estimated by a hand–object contact head and simple plane/object detectors, while a part-aware masked-view consistency regularizer stabilizes adaptation of fine-grained parts. result.text: The paper addresses the performance gap between low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full fine-tuning of foundation models, asking whether LoRA is being properly optimized. The key insight is that LoRA-based optimization is mathematically equivalent to full fine-tuning with a low-rank gradient, and that this low-rank gradient can be expressed directly from the gradients of LoRA’s two low-rank matrices; therefore, improving LoRA amounts to better approximating the full-fine-tuning gradient via adjustments to those matrix gradients. The authors propose LoRA-Pro, which derives and applies theoretically optimal adjustments to the low-rank matrix gradients so the resulting low-rank update more closely matches the full fine-tuning gradient, and they validate this approach across diverse tasks—showing substantial closing of the performance gap.

A horizontal scheduler allocates drafting effort to depths/nodes with high entropy or low coupling scores while a vertical, non‑autoregressive drafter proposes nodes in parallel, reducing wasted compute. result.text: ControlRouter is a training-free arbitration plugin for composable multi-modal control in text-to-image diffusion. The proposed Cascade Speculative Drafting (CS Drafting) introduces a Vertical Cascade that replaces neural autoregressive token-by-token generation with parallel or non-autoregressive drafting, and a Horizontal Cascade that dynamically prioritizes and allocates drafting time to more important or uncertain tokens; combined, these cascades let the target model accept larger portions of drafts less frequently and thus run fewer iterations.
